# Region Hovedstaden

Region Hovedstaden is one of Denmark's five administrative health regions and operates its own psychiatric service, Region Hovedstadens Psykiatri (RHP), which treats children, young people and adults with ADHD [^src10]. The region is one of the largest contributors of data to ADHD-DATABASEN, the Danish national clinical quality registry that tracks how well regions meet standardized indicators for ADHD assessment ("udredning") and treatment ("behandling") [^src16][^src22]. The region's defining significance in this dataset is a 24 % increase in the number of ADHD assessment courses over the reporting period, part of a nationwide rise seen in every region except Region Midtjylland [^src1].

In the annual report covering 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024, Region Hovedstaden's assessment volume grew substantially, from 196 to 228 courses, even as the region showed overall progress [^src4]. The region reported the highest overall indicator fulfillment of any region that year, at 36 %, while Region Midtjylland lay lowest at 7 % [^src7]. At the same time, the annual report noted that RHP did not meet the database's standards for its indicators overall, a result attributed mainly to inadequate registration practices rather than genuine clinical shortfalls [^src10]. Specific 2023-period results included 64 % (1,486 of 2,321 courses) reporting somatic examination [^src2], 46 % (971 of 2,093) on indicator 2b [^src4], 23 % (533 of 2,321) on indicator 3 [^src5], and 36 % (230 of 647) on indicator 4 [^src6]. On educational outcomes, 64 % of young people in the ADHD assessment population and 73 % in the treatment population passed their school-leaving exam before age 17 [^src8].

The following year's report (1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025) shows a more mixed picture. Alongside Region Midtjylland, Region Hovedstaden prioritized somatic examinations in line with new DMPG guidelines [^src11], and no departments in Hovedstaden, Sjælland or Nordjylland reached the development goal for indicator 1 [^src11]. The region reported registration problems for indicator 2a but reached 49 % on indicator 2b [^src12]. It recorded the lowest result nationally on indicator 3, at 20 % [^src13]. For indicator 4 (coordinating network meetings), Hovedstaden reached 29 % (556 of 1,905), tying with Region Syddanmark for the most network meetings held within the deadline of any region, though both remained far from the 90 % development goal, and Hovedstaden's results had been declining over the previous three reporting periods [^src14]. On indicator 5 (psychoeducation), the region scored 35 %, slightly ahead of Nordjylland's 33 % [^src15]. The region posted the largest improvement of any region on indicator 6 (medication), rising from 54 % to 67 % [^src15][^src16], and also recorded the highest share of young people passing their school-leaving exam among all regions [^src16]. The region continued to report difficulties registering the denominator population for treatment courses [^src17]. On the newly introduced adult indicator 9 (psychotherapy), Hovedstaden reached just 4 %, the highest rate among regions with at least three patients, reflecting the low national baseline of 1 % [^src18]. On indicator 10 (assessment of social support needs for adults), the region reached 49 % (151 of 311) [^src19]. On indicator 11 (adult medication within 120 days), Hovedstaden scored 37 %, substantially lower than other regions — a gap the report attributes mainly to registration difficulties in the region rather than real differences in clinical practice [^src20].

For the 2024–2025 period, Region Hovedstaden reported 2,183 ADHD assessment courses, 1,905 treatment courses for children and young people, and 311 treatment courses for adults, plus 118 assessment courses closed within 90 days due to a disproven suspicion of ADHD [^src21]. In its own commentary on the report, the region stated that RHP generally lies at or above the national average on most indicators even where the development goal is not met, welcomed proposed revisions to indicators 4 and 5, supported moving indicator 6 to supplementary material, and noted that adult psychiatry in the region is still adapting to a database that is new and not yet fully implemented in its workflows [^src22]. Within the region, specific clinical units named in the data include Bispebjerg's child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic [^src10] and PCK, a psychotherapeutic clinic, which achieved 9 % on indicator 9 [^src18].
